I'm looking at the user's question about optimizing their FR sourcebook PDFs for session content generation. They want to know if converting to Markdown would be better than their current approach, so I need to understand what they're working with—large reference files that are cited in their agents documentation but apparently not yet integrated into an efficient workflow.

Let me weigh the realistic options here. Leaving them as PDFs means I'd need a dedicated tool to extract and read them on demand, which I don't currently have access to in this environment. Converting to Markdown would make them searchable and linkable within their Obsidian vault, but D&D sourcebooks have complex formatting with stat blocks, sidebars, and maps that don't translate cleanly to plain text, plus there's the copyright consideration of storing extracted WotC content as files in their vault.

A full vector database feels like overkill for a single DM's personal campaign. The hybrid approach—converting to Markdown and organizing by topic or region so they can reference specific files via wikilinks—actually fits the Obsidian workflow best. But there's also the option of being selective: since this is specifically a Shadowdale campaign, I could focus on extracting just the relevant chapters and entries rather than the entire sourcebook.

The real constraint is that I don't have a PDF reader tool, and even if I did, loading a 30MB file repeatedly would be inefficient. So the practical path is to convert once using a solid extraction tool, split the output into logical chunks by chapter and section, then keep the original PDFs as visual reference while the agent works from the Markdown. This makes everything searchable and linkable within Obsidian.

The structure would organize the references by source and topic—campaign guide chapters in one folder, player's guide in another, with faction and location details nested underneath so the agent can pull only what's needed for the current session.

For extraction, `marker` is the cleanest option for D&D-style mixed layouts with tables and figures, though `pymupdf4llm` works fine for a quicker first pass. Either way, the agents.md file would need updating to point to the new Markdown structure as the primary source.

Short answer: **yes — convert them to Markdown once, organized by chapter/topic, and treat the MD as the agent's primary lookup with the PDFs kept as visual ground truth (maps, art, layout).** Reading 30 MB and 15 MB PDFs on every session is the wrong default for an Obsidian + agent workflow.

## Why MD beats PDF-on-demand here

- **Context cost.** A full FR sourcebook is 300–500 pages. No agent can keep both PDFs in context. Every query becomes "extract → re-tokenize → answer," which is slow and lossy.
- **No native PDF tool in this agent.** Right now I can `view` text files and grep them; I can't read these PDFs without running an extraction tool. Converting once removes that gap permanently.
- **Obsidian-native.** Once it's MD, `codebase-retrieval`, plain `grep`, and Obsidian's graph/wikilinks all work against the sourcebook. You can `[[harpers]]` from `factions.md` and have it resolve into the canonical entry.
- **Topic granularity.** `agents.md`'s reference patterns (location lookup, NPC lookup, faction lookup, deity, regional encounter tables) all want narrow slices, not whole books. Splitting by chapter makes those slices cheap to retrieve.

## Trade-offs to know

- **Extraction quality is uneven.** Sidebars, stat blocks, two-column layouts, and inline maps don't always survive cleanly. You should expect a small cleanup pass on the chapters you actually use most (Dalelands, Zhentarim, Harpers, the relevant deities for your party).
- **Maps and art largely don't translate.** Keep the PDFs in `references/` for those. The MD is for *text* canon.
- **Vault size grows.** Roughly 1–2 MB of text per book, fanned out into ~30–50 files each. Negligible for Obsidian; just worth knowing.
- **Copyright posture.** Extracting WotC text into your personal vault for DM use is the same posture as already storing the PDFs. No change in practice, but worth being aware that you're materializing the prose.

## Recommended structure

```
references/
├── forgotten-realms-campaign-guide.pdf      # kept — visual ground truth
├── forgotten-realms-players-guide.pdf       # kept — visual ground truth
├── campaign-guide/
│   ├── 00-overview.md
│   ├── regions/        # dalelands.md, cormyr.md, sword-coast.md, ...
│   ├── factions/       # harpers.md, zhentarim.md, lords-alliance.md, ...
│   ├── deities/
│   ├── monsters.md
│   └── adventure-hooks.md
└── players-guide/
    ├── 00-overview.md
    ├── cosmology.md
    ├── races.md
    ├── deities.md
    └── major-cities.md
```

Then `agents.md`'s source hierarchy becomes: campaign files → `references/*.md` (primary lookup, wikilinkable) → original PDFs (only when you need a map or layout) → general 5e knowledge.

## Tooling options for the one-time conversion

- **`pymupdf4llm`** — fast, simple, decent markdown, handles prose well. Good first pass.
- **`marker-pdf`** (datalab-to/marker) — currently best-in-class for mixed layouts, tables, sidebars. Slower, cleaner output. Better for stat blocks.
- **`docling`** (IBM) — also strong, produces structured JSON or MD.

For two books, `marker-pdf` is what I'd reach for; `pymupdf4llm` if you want it done in five minutes and are willing to accept rougher stat-block layout.

## What I'd suggest as a first move

A staged, opt-in path so you don't pay for chapters you'll never use:

1. **Extract both books with `marker-pdf`** into `references/campaign-guide/_raw/` and `references/players-guide/_raw/` (one MD per chapter, plus an `images/` folder).
2. **Hand-curate the high-traffic chapters first** — Dalelands region, the four-or-five factions you'll actually use, the deities your PCs care about. Move them out of `_raw/` into the clean structure above.
3. **Update `agents.md`** to point at `references/*.md` as the primary lookup, with the PDFs demoted to "visual reference only."
4. **Leave the long tail in `_raw/`** — still grep-able by the agent, just not pretty.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract a PDF to Markdown using pymupdf4llm.

Writes:
  <out_dir>/full.md            — single concatenated markdown
  <out_dir>/pages/page-NNNN.md — one file per page (for chapter splitting later)
  <out_dir>/images/            — extracted figures/maps

Usage:
  python scripts/extract_pdf.py <pdf_path> <out_dir>
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import pymupdf4llm


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2

    pdf_path = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
    out_dir = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()
    if not pdf_path.exists():
        print(f"error: {pdf_path} does not exist", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    pages_dir = out_dir / "pages"
    images_dir = out_dir / "images"
    pages_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    images_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    print(f"extracting {pdf_path.name} -> {out_dir}")
    t0 = time.time()

    # page_chunks=True returns a list of dicts, one per page, with 'text' and metadata.
    # write_images=True extracts figures into image_path.
    chunks = pymupdf4llm.to_markdown(
        str(pdf_path),
        page_chunks=True,
        write_images=True,
        image_path=str(images_dir),
        image_format="png",
        dpi=150,
        show_progress=True,
    )

    full_md_parts: list[str] = []
    for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks, start=1):
        text = chunk.get("text", "") if isinstance(chunk, dict) else str(chunk)
        page_file = pages_dir / f"page-{i:04d}.md"
        page_file.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        full_md_parts.append(f"<!-- page {i} -->\n\n{text}\n")

    full_md = "\n".join(full_md_parts)
    (out_dir / "full.md").write_text(full_md, encoding="utf-8")

    elapsed = time.time() - t0
    print(
        f"done in {elapsed:.1f}s · {len(chunks)} pages · "
        f"{len(full_md):,} chars · "
        f"{sum(1 for _ in images_dir.iterdir())} images"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

The lore itself—geography, factions, deities—remains largely compatible, but the timeline is locked at 1479 DR, and major events like the Second Sundering, Mystra's return, and Netheril's fall haven't happened yet in these books. The stat blocks are entirely unusable for 5e, and if they want to align with current 5e canon (1492+ DR), they'll need to reframe the setting and account for those retconned plot points.

Before I reorganize anything, I need to surface this finding clearly and let them decide whether they want to keep using these 4e books for lore depth, switch to 5e-era sourcebooks like the Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide, or blend both approaches.

Extraction is done. Both books converted, and there's one important finding before we go further with the reorg.

## Headline finding: these are 4th Edition books, not 5e

Page 109's Dalelands prose names the year as **1479 DR (Year of the Ageless One)**, and the credits explicitly call out the **4th Edition revision guide by Bruce R. Cordell, Richard Baker, and Philip Athans**. The encounter design uses 4e syntax (`Level 3 Controller (Leader)`, "Goblin Hexer (H)"), and a search for "Armor Class" across the entire 30 MB PDF returns zero hits — confirmed, this is the **2008 Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide** for D&D 4e, not a 5e source.

Why it matters for the campaign:

- **Timeline:** locked at 1479 DR (post-Spellplague, pre-Sundering). Current 5e canon sits at 1492+ DR with the Spellplague healed, Mystra restored, Netheril gone, and the dales rearranged. If you want the campaign to align with 5e's "current state of the Realms," you'll either reframe events forward or accept the campaign sits in the 4e era.
- **Lore is still ~80% usable:** geography hasn't moved, the Dalelands prose is excellent, Harpers/Zhentarim/Cult of the Dragon still exist, Greenwood-style deity entries still apply broadly. The dale-by-dale political summary on page 109 is genuinely good source material for Shadowdale.
- **Mechanics are 0% usable for 5e:** stat blocks, encounter levels, racial powers, and rituals all need to be discarded. The agent should never copy mechanical content from these PDFs into a 5e session.

If you want a 5e-native FR reference, **Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide (2015)** is the canonical companion. Worth grabbing before deciding the reorg structure.

## Extraction quality (pymupdf4llm)

**What came out clean (the 80% case — prose lookup):**

- Region overviews like the Dalelands page (109) extracted as readable prose with proper paragraph structure, italicized dale names, and DC-skill-check call-outs intact.
- Headings mostly survived — chapter and region boundaries are detectable.

**What's noisy (skip or rework):**

- **TOC pages** (campaign guide pages 4–5) are dotted-leader soup — `. . . . . . 76`. Throw them out, the chapter MD files give you structure already.
- **Stat blocks render as strikethrough-wrapped headings** (`## ~~**Goblin Hexer (H)**~~`) because pymupdf reads the colored stat-block bands as strikethrough. They're recoverable as text but won't be useful as 5e mechanics anyway, see above.
- **Heading hierarchy is unreliable.** Bold body text occasionally got promoted to `## H2`. Don't trust H1/H2 levels for navigation; trust the per-page filenames and search.
- **Tables sometimes flatten into pipe-soup** (the contents page is the worst case). Most regional sidebar tables are still readable.
- **Image alt-text is empty.** OK for prose lookup, but the agent can't reason about maps from MD alone — the original PDFs stay as visual ground truth.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| campaign-guide/_raw/ | 298 | 1.25 M | 481 | 119 MB |
| players-guide/_raw/ | 162 | 0.65 M | 212 | 54 MB |

The text MD itself is small (~2 MB combined); the bulk is extracted images. If iCloud sync size is a concern, the `images/` directories are the lever.

## Files I created

- `scripts/extract_pdf.py` — small reusable extraction script. Keep it if you want to extract more PDFs later (e.g., SCAG once you have it); say the word and I'll remove it.
- `references/campaign-guide/_raw/` — full.md + pages/ + images/

The prose came out fine, and the things `marker` would clean up — stat blocks, sidebars, tables — are the parts we're either discarding (stat blocks: 4e) or low-value for our use (tables). I'd save the time and curate the 80% useful prose by hand instead.

I'm noticing a temporal inconsistency in the campaign materials — World.md explicitly references 4e-era canon like Mystra's death and the Spellplague's aftermath, but the stat blocks are pulling from 5e Monster Manual sources, which suggests the campaign might be mixing editions or the materials were updated at different times.

The user said "5e canon" but the actual campaign files point to a 4e-era setting with 5e mechanics, which is a pretty common hybrid approach for Forgotten Realms DMs. I should clarify whether they meant 5e mechanically or if they actually want the post-Sundering 1492+ DR timeline, since that would require significant rewrites to the world file. If it's the former, the 4e Campaign Guide materials I extracted would be nearly perfect for the setting and lore, and I can proceed with the reorganization while curating the Dalelands, factions, and deities from those sources. efly and proceed. I'll note the finding, propose the straightforward resolution—5e mechanics with the 4e-era setting the campaign already has—and then define exactly what pages from the campaign guide I'll curate so they can approve the plan before I start reorganizing files. I'm looking at pulling regional entries like the Dalelands, Cormyr, and Sembia, plus faction and threat lore around the Drow, Netheril, and Church of Shar, along with the pantheon chapter to ground the setting properly.

Given the active campaign threads—the Drow conflict under Old Skull, the Harpers connection, the Netheril shadow from the north, and the Feywild bleed—I should prioritize the highest-impact files first: the Dalelands region itself, Cormyr as a neighbor, a combined Drow and Vhaeraun entry, Netheril as the looming threat, and deity entries for the gods most relevant to what's happening in the campaign. That's maybe 5-6 files to start with rather than all 20-25 at once, so I can get sign-off on the structure before diving into the full reorganization.

Found something important before doing the reorg. Pausing to surface it.

## The campaign is already 4e-era setting + 5e mechanics

`campaign/world.md` explicitly establishes:

- **"Mystra is dead"** (lore callout)
- **"the Spellplague's aftermath means magic sometimes behaves unexpectedly"**
- **"Fey have flooded its forests since Mystra's fall thinned the border with the Feywild"**

That is **exactly the 4e-era state of the Realms (1479 DR)** — the very era covered by the campaign-guide PDF we just extracted. Meanwhile your statline reference for Quillip is `MM p.253; CR 1/4` — 5e Monster Manual page numbers and CR notation. So the campaign is, by design, **5e mechanically + 4e-era setting state**.

If "5e canon" meant *5e current timeline* (1492+ DR, Sundering complete, Mystra restored, Netheril gone), that would contradict everything in `world.md` and require a substantial rewrite of the campaign bible. I don't think that's what you meant — but flagging it because the answer matters for what we do next.

## What I think you actually meant

> "5e *rules and stat blocks*. Setting era is what `world.md` already says it is — late 4e, ~1479 DR, post-Spellplague, Mystra dead, Sundering hasn't happened (or hasn't fully landed) here."

If that's right, the two PDFs we extracted are **a near-perfect fit for setting/lore** — Greenwood himself wrote the Dalelands page that mentions Shadowdale, the dead-Mystra cosmology, the drow stirring beneath Old Skull. We just have to be disciplined about where we use the 4e source:

| Use the 4e PDFs for | Don't use the 4e PDFs for |
|---|---|
| Geography, regions, dale-by-dale identity | Stat blocks (4e powers, defenses) |
| Faction lore (Harpers, Zhentarim, Netheril, Cult of the Dragon) | Encounter levels, XP budgets |
| Deity flavor and dogma | Skill DCs, ritual mechanics |
| NPC flavor and naming conventions | Magic items as written |
| Cosmology, the Spellplague, Plaguelands | Class/race mechanics from the Player's Guide |

**Confirm this read** ("5e mechanics, 4e-era setting, 4e PDFs are valid for lore-only") and I'll proceed with the reorg.

## Proposed Phase 1 curation (5 files)

Targeting only what's directly hot in the current campaign:

| File | Source pages | Why first |
|---|---|---|
| `references/campaign-guide/regions/dalelands.md` | 108–113 | Shadowdale lives here — primary lookup |
| `references/campaign-guide/regions/cormyr.md` | 104–107 | Southern neighbor, Purple Dragon Knights are a recurring lever |
| `references/campaign-guide/threats/netheril.md` | 260–263 | Looming northern shadow per `world.md`; Shar tie |
| `references/campaign-guide/factions/drow.md` | 248–251 | Lolth vs Vhaeraun war is the active arc; pull Vhaeraun exarch entry from p. 78 |
| `references/campaign-guide/deities/_index.md` | 70–81 | One-paragraph entries for the seven deities listed in `world.md` (Mielikki, Silvanus, Selûne, Oghma, Shar, Cyric, Lolth) |

Each file will:
- Get a header callout: source (4e Campaign Guide, page range), era note (1479 DR, Mystra dead), and a "use for lore only — stat in 5e" reminder.
- Reproduce the 4e prose verbatim where it's clean (Greenwood's writing is the value), with TOC dotted-leader noise stripped.
- Cross-link to existing campaign files where they already define canon (e.g., `[[world]]`, `[[geography]]`, `[[factions]]`).

Phase 2 (deferred — Sembia, Waterdeep, Cormanthor, Cult of the Dragon, Church of Shar, individual deity pages, etc.) gets curated only when an upcoming session actually needs them. Phase 3 — everything else — stays in `_raw/` for grep-only access.

After Phase 1, I'll update `agents.md` to:
1. Add an explicit **Edition note** section (4e setting era + 5e mechanics).
2. Re-point the source hierarchy: campaign files → curated `references/campaign-guide/{regions,factions,deities,threats}/*.md` → `_raw/` chapter pages → original PDFs (visual only) → general 5e knowledge.

## One thing I'd add

`references/_raw/` material is bulky (173 MB total, mostly extracted PNGs). Suggest adding to `.gitignore`:

```
.venv/
references/*/_raw/images/
```

Keeps the per-page MD in version control (small, useful for grep) while letting the heavy image extraction stay local-only — the original PDFs in `references/*.pdf` remain the visual ground truth, and they're already committed.

**Confirm "5e mechanics + 4e-era setting + Phase 1 file list looks right"** and I'll start the curation. If you want a different file mix for Phase 1, name swaps and I'll adjust before doing any writes.
